3120.h: 277 - Abū al-Walīd al-Faqīh Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad *
3120.t:
The unique Imam (الإمام), the hadith master (الحافظ), the mufti (المفتي), the shaykh of Khurasan, Abū al-Walīd Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Hārūn al-Naysābūrī, al-Shāfiʿī, the devout worshipper (العابد). ⟦15:492⟧
He was born: after 270 AH.
He heard from: أبي عبد الله محمد بن إبراهيم البوشنجي، وابن خزيمة، وعدة ببلده، والحسن بن سفيان بنسا، وأحمد بن الحسن بن عبد الجبار الصوفي ببغداد، وهذه الطبقة.
He studied jurisprudence under Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn Surayj, and he is the holder of a recognised view (wajh) within the school.
Among the strangest things he came out with is that he said: whoever repeats al-Fātiḥah twice, his prayer is invalid; and this is contrary to the explicit text of the Imam (الإمام).
He said: cupping breaks the fast of both the one who cups and the one who is cupped, and he held that this is the position of the school because of the authenticity of the hadiths on it.
There is room for objection here, because the Imam (الإمام) (1) did not declare the hadiths weak (ضعيف); rather, he claimed that they were abrogated (2) . ⟦15:493⟧
Narrating from him: الحاكم، وابن مندة، وأبو طاهر بن محمش، والقاضي أحمد بن الحسن الحيري، وأبو الفضل أحمد بن محمد السهلي الصفار، وعدة.
Al-Ḥākim said: Abū al-Walīd compiled (al-Mustakhraj ʿalā Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)
and he compiled (al-Aḥkām) according to the school of al-Shāfiʿī (1) .
Abū Saʿd the man of letters (الأديب) said: I asked Abū ʿAlī al-Thaqafī, saying: whom shall we ask after you?
He said: Abū al-Walīd (2) .
Al-Ḥākim said: I heard the master Abū al-Walīd say: my father said to me: what are you compiling?
I said: I am compiling a mustakhraj on (the Book of al-Bukhārī) .
He said: you should take (the Book of Muslim) , for it has more blessing, since al-Bukhārī was associated with the position on the utterance (al-lafẓ) (3) .
Muḥammad ibn al-Dhuhlī said: Muslim too was associated with the utterance; do you not see how he rose from the session of al-Dhuhlī in front of the whole assembly when he said: let whoever holds the view of Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl not come near us?
This is a difficult question. Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and others did not approve of delving into this question, even though al-Bukhārī (may Allah have mercy on him) never stated that explicitly, nor did he say: our utterances of the Qurʾān are created.
Rather, he said: our acts are created, and what is recited and uttered is the speech of Allah the Exalted, and it is not created; so refraining from expansive expressions is safer for a person. ⟦15:494⟧
This Abū al-Walīd was one of the pillars of the religion.
When he died, Abū Ṭāhir ibn Maḥmish the jurist (الفقيه), one of his students, elegised him in a poem of sixty verses (1) .
Al-Ḥākim said: Abū al-Walīd showed us the engraving of his seal ring: Allah is the trust of Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad.
He said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAdī showed us the engraving of his seal ring: Allah is the trust of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad.
He said: al-Rabīʿ showed us the engraving of his seal ring: Allah is the trust of al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān.
He said: the engraving of al-Shāfiʿī's seal ring was: Allah is the trust of Muḥammad ibn Idrīs (2) .
This chain of transmission (الإسناد) is firmly established.
Abū al-Walīd died: in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, in the year 349 AH, aged 72.
Al-Ḥākim said: he is Abū al-Walīd al-Qurashī al-Umawī al-Shāfiʿī, the Imam (الإمام) of the people of hadith in Khurasan, the most ascetic of the scholars I have seen and the most devoted of them to worship; he studied jurisprudence in Baghdad under Ibn Surayj (3) .
I say: Among those who died in the same year as him: the scholar of Isfahan, the judge (القاضي) Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAssāl; the hadith master (الحافظ) of Khurasan, Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Zayd al-Naysābūrī; the musnid (المسند) of the age in Egypt, Abū al-Fawāris Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Sindī al-Ṣābūnī; the musnid (المسند) of Baghdad, Aḥmad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Yaḥyā al-Adamī al-ʿAṭashī; Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Khurāsānī; the musnid (المسند) of Damascus, Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ Sinān al-Makhzūmī; the shaykh of the reciters (القارئ), Abū Ṭāhir ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Abī Hāshim; the long-lived ⟦15:495⟧ Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmrawayh ibn ʿIlm al-Ṣaffār; and Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Nīkhāb al-Ṭībī in Baghdad.
أخبرنا أحمد بن هبة الله، أنبأنا القاسم بن عبد الله الصفار، أخبرتنا عائشة بنت أحمد، أخبرنا الحسن بن علي البستي، أخبرنا يحيى بن إبراهيم المزكي، حدثنا الزاهد إمام عصره أبو الوليد حسان بن محمد الفقيه، حدثنا أبو عبد الله البوشنجي، حدثنا يحيى بن بكير، حدثني الليث، عن ابن الهاد، عن ابن شهاب، عن عروة، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate in his prayer: (O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the False Messiah, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and death; O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and from debt) (1) the hadith.

1132.h: 133 - Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hamdānī * (ع)
1132.t:
The hadith master (الحافظ), the Imam (الإمام), the authority (الحجة), Abū Yūsuf al-Hamdānī, al-Sabīʿī, al-Kūfī.
He narrated much from: his grandfather.
He also narrated from: زياد بن علاقة، وآدم بن علي، وآدم بن سليمان أبي يحيى، وإسماعيل السدي، وعاصم بن بهدلة، وعبد الكريم الجزري، وإبراهيم بن عبد الأعلى، وعبد الأعلى بن عامر الثعلبي، وأشعث بن أبي الشعثاء، وثوير بن أبي فاختة، وسعد أبي مجاهد الطائي، وسعيد بن مسروق، وسماك بن حرب، وعامر بن شقيق بن جمرة الأسدي، وعبد العزيز بن رفيع، وعثمان بن عاصم، ومخارق الأحمسي، ومنصور بن المعتمر، وخلق كثير. ⟦7:355⟧
He was one of the vessels of hadith, and one of the shaykhs of Islam, like his father, his grandfather, and his brother ʿĪsā.
Narrating from him: أخوه، وحجاج الأعور، وأحمد بن خالد الوهبي، وآدم بن أبي إياس، وعبد الرزاق، ومحمد بن سابق، وشبابة، وإسحاق بن منصور السلولي، وأحمد بن يونس، وحسين بن محمد المروذي، وعبد الله بن رجاء، وأبو نعيم، ومحمد بن كثير العبدي، وأبو غسان النهدي، ومحمد بن يوسف الفريابي، وأبو سلمة التبوذكي، ويحيى بن أبي كثير، ووكيع، ويحيى بن آدم، وعلي بن الجعد، ومعاوية بن عمرو الأزدي، وأبو الوليد الطيالسي، وخلق كثير.
Hārūn ibn Ḥātim narrated from Dubays ibn Ḥumayd: that Isrāʾīl was born in the year 100 AH.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus, who said:
Isrāʾīl said to me: I used to memorise the hadith of Abū Isḥāq as I memorise a sūrah of the Qurʾān.
Ibn al-Madīnī, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, who said: Isrāʾīl is above Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh.
Ḥarb al-Kirmānī narrated from Aḥmad, who said: he was reliable (ثقة); and he began to marvel at his memory.
As for Ṣāliḥ ibn Aḥmad, he narrated from his father, who said: Isrāʾīl from Abū Isḥāq: in it he is somewhat soft in hadith (لين الحديث); he heard from him late in life.
Abū Ṭālib said: Aḥmad was asked: which of the two is more firmly reliable (ثبت): Sharīk or Isrāʾīl?
He said: Isrāʾīl used to convey what he heard; he was more firmly reliable (ثبت) than Sharīk.
I said: who is dearer to you regarding Abū Isḥāq: Yūnus or his son Isrāʾīl?
He said: Isrāʾīl, because he had a book.
Al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh: who is dearer to you regarding Abū Isḥāq: Yūnus or Isrāʾīl?
He said: Yūnus. ⟦7:356⟧
Abū Dāwūd said: I said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal (1) : when Isrāʾīl is alone in narrating a hadith, is he used as proof (يحتج به)?
He said: Isrāʾīl is firmly reliable (ثبت) in hadith; Yaḥyā used to be hard on him on account of Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt.
He said: he narrated from him things that are rejected (المنكر) (2) .
Then Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated nothing at all from him.
Aḥmad said: when Isrāʾīl narrated from his book, he would leave nothing out, and he memorised from his book.
In one report from Aḥmad, he said: Sharīk is more exact than Isrāʾīl regarding Abū Isḥāq.
ʿAbbās narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, who said: al-Qaṭṭān would not narrate from Isrāʾīl, nor from Sharīk.
Ibn Maʿīn said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam said: we used to write in Isrāʾīl's presence from his memory.
Yaḥyā said: Isrāʾīl did not used to memorise, then he memorised afterwards -meaning: that he studied his book-.
Yaḥyā said: Isrāʾīl is more firmly reliable (ثبت) regarding Abū Isḥāq than Shaybān.
Aḥmad ibn Zuhayr and others narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn: reliable (ثقة).
Al-ʿIjlī said: reliable (ثقة).
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said: reliable (ثقة), truthful (صدوق), one of the most meticulous of the associates of Abū Isḥāq.
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah said: truthful (صدوق), and not the strongest.
He also said once: he is somewhat soft in hadith (لين الحديث).
Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Ḥuddānī said: I heard ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus say:
Our associates Sufyān and Sharīk ... and he counted some people, when they disagreed about the hadith of Abū Isḥāq, would come to my father, and he would say: go to my son Isrāʾīl, for he narrates more from him than I do, ⟦7:357⟧
and is more meticulous in it than I am; and he was the one who led his grandfather.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Thalj narrated from Shabābah:
I said to Yūnus: dictate to me the hadith of your father.
He said: write from Isrāʾīl, for my father dictated it to him.
الحسين بن عبد الرحمن الجرجرائي: عن خلف بن تميم، سمعت أبا الأحوص - إن شاء الله - ذكر عن أبي إسحاق، قال:
Isrāʾīl left us no niche and no basket without stuffing it (1) with books.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥunaynī: I heard Abū Nuʿaym being asked: which of the two is more firmly reliable (ثبت): Isrāʾīl or Abū ʿAwānah?
He said: Isrāʾīl.
Al-Nasāʾī said: no harm in him (لا بأس به).
I say: The majority praised Isrāʾīl, and the two Shaykhs adduced him as proof; he was a hadith master (الحافظ), a man of books and of knowledge.
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Barāʾ narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī: Isrāʾīl is weak (ضعيف).
I say: ʿAlī followed his teacher Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, and Abū Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm followed in their footsteps and said: weak (ضعيف).
He went to his hadiths that are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين) , rejected them and held them not to be used as proof (يحتج به); no attention is to be paid to that; rather, he is reliable (ثقة).
Yes, in firmness he is not like Sufyān and Shuʿbah, but perhaps he comes close to them in the hadith of his grandfather, for he kept to him morning and evening for ten years; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to narrate from him and strengthen him, and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd achieved nothing by abandoning narration from him while narrating from Mujālid (2) . ⟦7:358⟧
ʿAbbās narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, who said:
Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah, Zuhayr and Isrāʾīl: their hadith regarding Abū Isḥāq is nearly equal; the true associates of Abū Isḥāq are only Sufyān and Shuʿbah.
ʿAbbās al-Dūrī said: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying:
Isrāʾīl came to Baghdad and the people gathered around him; he was seated above a raised place, and a man with a notebook stood up and began asking him from it, without the people looking into it; when Isrāʾīl had finished, that man sat down and dictated it to the people (1) .
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to say: Isrāʾīl is more firmly reliable (ثبت) regarding Abū Isḥāq than Shuʿbah and al-Thawrī.
I say: this is what I incline to more than what preceded, for Isrāʾīl was his grandfather's walking staff, and along with his knowledge and memory he was a man of righteousness and humility (may Allah have mercy on him); his brother ʿĪsā was more meticulous than he, more learned, and more devout (may Allah be pleased with both of them).
Abū Aḥmad ibn ʿAdī made his biography long (2) , and listed for him several gharīb (الغريب) hadiths.
It has reached us that Shaqīq al-Balkhī said:
I learned humility from Isrāʾīl; we would be around him and he would not know who was on his right or who was on his left, because of his reflection on the Hereafter, so I knew that he was a righteous man.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān said: Isrāʾīl is above Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh.
It was said to Yaḥyā: Isrāʾīl narrated three hundred from Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, and three hundred from Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt?
He said: the fault did not come from him; it came from both of them (3) . ⟦7:359⟧
I say: he is alluding to Ibn Muhājir and al-Qattāt being soft in hadith (لين الحديث).
Among the gharīb (الغريب) reports of Isrāʾīl: Aḥmad narrated in (his Musnad) , حدثنا أبو سعيد، حدثنا إسرائيل، حدثنا سعيد بن مسروق، عن سعد بن عبيدة، عن ابن عمر:
From ʿUmar, that he said: No, by my father.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Stop! Whoever swears by anything other than Allah has committed shirk (1)) .
Its narrators are reliable (ثقة).
Among his elevated chains (العالي): أنبأنا عبد الرحمن بن قدامة الفقيه، أنبأنا عمر بن محمد، أنبأنا هبة الله بن محمد، أنبأنا محمد بن محمد بن غيلان، حدثنا أبو بكر الشافعي، حدثنا إبراهيم بن عبد الرحيم بن دنوقا، حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح العجلي، حدثنا إسرائيل، عن أبي إسحاق، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، عن ابن مسعود، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to recite: (“Indeed, I am the Provider, the Possessor of Strength, the Firm” (Qurʾān 51:58) (2)) .
This is a gharīb (الغريب) hadith.
Abū Nuʿaym al-Mulāʾī and Qaʿnab ibn al-Muḥarrar said: Isrāʾīl died in the year 160 AH.
Ibn Saʿd and Shabāb (3) al-ʿUṣfurī said: he died in the year 162 AH. ⟦7:360⟧
Muṭayyan said: he died in the year one.

4116.h: 40 - al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā al-Baghdādī Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn *
4116.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the eminent scholar (العلامة), the shaykh of the Ḥanbalīs, the judge (القاضي) Abū Yaʿlā Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Khalaf ibn Aḥmad al-Baghdādī, al-Ḥanbalī, Ibn al-Farrāʾ, author of the great (al-Taʿlīqah) and of the useful works in the school.
He was born: at the beginning of the year 380 AH.
He heard: علي بن عمر الحربي، وإسماعيل بن سويد، وأبا القاسم بن حبابة، وعيسى بن الوزير، وابن أخي ميمي، وأم الفتح بنت أحمد بن كامل، وأبا طاهر المخلص، وأبا الطيب بن منتاب، وابن معروف القاضي، وطائفة.
He held several dictation sessions (الأمالي).
Narrating from him: الخطيب، وأبو الخطاب الكلوذاني، وأبو الوفاء بن عقيل، وأبو غالب بن البناء، وأخوه يحيى بن البناء، وأبو العز بن كادش، وأبو بكر محمد بن عبد الباقي، وابنه القاضي أبو الحسين محمد بن محمد ⟦18:89⟧ بن الفراء، وأبو سعد أحمد بن محمد الزوزني.
Among the earlier ones, the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ) Abū ʿAlī al-Ahwāzī also narrated from him.
He gave legal opinions (الفتوى) and taught, and the members of the school trained under him; leadership in jurisprudence (الفقه) culminated in him, and he was the scholar of Iraq in his time, together with knowledge of the sciences of the Qurʾān and its exegesis (التفسير), of disputation and of legal theory. His father was one of the notables of the Ḥanafīs and one of the witnesses of the court at the capital; he died when Abū Yaʿlā was ten years old, so his teacher, a Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ), taught him the acts of worship from (al-Mukhtaṣar) of al-Khiraqī; jurisprudence (الفقه) became delightful to him, and he moved to the study circle of Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid (1) , the shaykh of the Ḥanbalīs, kept his company for years and excelled in jurisprudence (الفقه) under him; at his command he took up teaching in the year 402 AH, and his first direct hearing (السماع) was from ʿAlī ibn Maʿrūf in the year (385) AH.
He also heard in Mecca, and in Damascus from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Naṣr, and in Aleppo. He compiled the book (Ibṭāl Taʾwīl al-Ṣifāt), and they rose against him because of the flimsy and the fabricated (الموضوع) material in it; then the creed that al-Qādir bi-Allāh had compiled was brought out from him to the scholars, and the book (Ibṭāl al-Taʾwīl) was carried to al-Qādir, who liked it; and there occurred affairs and tribulations - we ask Allah for well-being - then the vizier ʿAlī ibn al-Muslimah made peace between the two parties, and said before the assembly: the Qurʾān is the speech of Allah, and the reports about the attributes are passed on as they came (2) .
Then Abū Yaʿlā was appointed to the judgeship of the Abode of the Caliphate and al-Ḥarīm, together with the judgeship of Harran (3) and Ḥulwān (4) . He had recited the ten recitation traditions (القراءات), and he was a man of worship and night vigil, and of constant ⟦18:90⟧ application to writing, together with majesty and dignity; he did not have a long reach in the knowledge of hadith, so he sometimes adduced flimsy material as proof.
Studying jurisprudence under him: أبو الحسن البغدادي، وأبو جعفر الهاشمي، وأبو الغنائم بن الغباري، وأبو علي بن البناء، وأبو الوفاء بن القواس، وأبو الحسن النهري، وابن عقيل، وأبو الخطاب، وأبو الحسن بن جدا، وأبو يعلى الكيال، وأبو الفرج الشيرازي.
He wrote the book (Aḥkām al-Qurʾān) , and (Masāʾil al-Īmān) , and (al-Muʿtamad) and its abridgement, and (al-Muqtabas) , and (ʿUyūn al-Masāʾil) , and (al-Radd ʿalā al-Karrāmiyyah) , and (al-Radd ʿalā al-Sālimiyyah wa-al-Mujassimah) , and (al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah) , and (al-Kalām fī al-Istiwāʾ) , and (al-ʿUddah) on the principles of jurisprudence (أصول الفقه) (1) ; and its abridgement, and (Faḍāʾil Aḥmad) , and the book (al-Ṭibb) , and many other works which I have listed in (Tārīkh al-Islām (2)) .
He was abstinent, pure of soul, of great standing, and of solid scrupulousness.
He died: in the year 458 AH.
In that year died: al-Bayhaqī (3) ; the judge (القاضي) of Sāriyah, Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Sarawī (4) ; Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Ghālib the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ); Abū al-Ṭayyib ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn Shammah (5) ; Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Sīdah (6) - author of ⟦18:91⟧ (al-Muḥkam) - and the judge (القاضي) Abū ʿĀṣim Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAbbādī in Herat (1) .

2327.h: 115 - Ibn Bulbul al-Shaybānī Abū al-Ṣaqr Ismāʿīl **
2327.t:
The great vizier, the unique one, the man of letters (الأديب), Abū al-Ṣaqr Ismāʿīl ibn Bulbul al-Shaybānī. ⟦13:199⟧
One of the poets, the eloquent, and the generous who were much praised.
He became vizier to al-Muʿtamid in the year 265 AH, after al-Ḥasan ibn Makhlad (1) ; then he was dismissed, then became vizier again, then was dismissed, then became vizier a third time upon the arrest of Ṣāʿid the vizier, in the year 72.
He was of the rank of great kings, with an enormous allowance: each day a hundred sheep, seventy kids and a qinṭār of sweets; when al-Muʿtaḍid became heir apparent, he arrested him and tortured him until he perished in the year 278 AH.
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭāhir said: al-Muwaffaq's choice for his vizierate fell on Abū al-Ṣaqr, and he made vizier a man whose like has rarely been seen: in competence for important matters and independence in affairs, most effective in carrying out administration along its soundest paths, most beneficial in its results, and most protective of the sultan's affairs; along with his raising the standing of literature and its people, and his lavishing precious gifts on them; together with courage, high aspiration, and the smallness of this world in his eyes, except what he sent ahead for his Hereafter; along with the breadth of his forbearance and his restraint of anger, and his generosity towards those who sought to destroy him.
Abū ʿAlī al-Tanūkhī said: حدثنا أبو الحسين عبد الله بن أحمد، حدثنا سليمان بن الحسن قال:
Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Furāt said: I attended the session of Ibn Bulbul when he held a public sitting; the petitioners against injustice came in to him and he looked into their affairs, and none of them left without a gift, or an appointment, or the fulfilment of a need, or redress. A man remained at the end of the session asking him to waive the rent of his village.
He said: al-Muwaffaq has ordered that I waive nothing except by his command, so I shall inform him.
He said: the man appealed to us again and said: if the vizier puts me off, my situation will be ruined.
He said to his secretary: write his request in the memorandum.
The man turned away, not ⟦13:200⟧ far, then came back and asked permission to speak, then said:
Not in every reign and every age ... are deeds of kindness made easy
So if they become possible for you one day of time ... then hasten with them before the turns of fortune
He said to me: O Abū al-ʿAbbās: write for him the waiver of the rent of his estate this very hour.
And he ordered the money-changer to pay him five hundred dinars.
It is said that his page handed him the pen dipped in ink, and it dripped onto a costly robe, and the page took fright; he said: do not be alarmed, then he recited:
When musk perfumes the scent of a people ... the scent of ink suffices me
For nothing is finer than garments ... on whose edges lie the charcoal marks of black
I say: he spoke the truth, and it is a beauty spot on the garments of viziers.
Jaḥẓah (1) said: I composed:
Upon us, through Abū al-Ṣaqr ... are the great blessings of Allah
A king in whose eyes this world, ... for one who hopes from him, is little
So he ordered two hundred dinars for me.
Al-Ṣūlī said: Ibn Bulbul was born in the year 230 AH, and I saw him several times; he was of the utmost handsomeness and of perfect stature and build. He was arrested in Ṣafar of the year 78, fettered, and dressed in a cloak dipped in date syrup and trotter broth, and seated in a ⟦13:201⟧ hot place, and tortured with all kinds of torture, and he died in Jumādā al-Ūlā.
It was said: he was seen in a dream, and was asked: what did Allah do with you?
He said: He forgave me for what I suffered; He was not going to combine for me the punishment of this world and of the Hereafter.
وروى أبو علي التنوخي، عن أبيه، عن جماعة من أهل الحضرة أخبروه:
That al-Muʿtaḍid gave orders concerning Ibn Bulbul, and a large tub (1) was made for him and filled with white lead which was moistened; then his head was put into it up to his neck, and it was held down on him until he went still, and his spirit kept leaving with flatulence from his lower end until he died.
